name: PTY WebSocket origin and token boundary
instruction: PTY WebSocket attach paths must require both an allowed extension Origin and a one-time attach token before exposing a terminal session.
relevant_when: Go file that defines the PTY WebSocket handler, WebSocket upgrader, allowedOrigin check, attach token issuance, or token redemption for tty.create or tty.attach.
context: README.md (Security) states terminal WebSocket connections use the extension's origin and a one-time attach token obtained over native messaging, and that a token expires when used, when replaced by a newer token for that terminal, or when the native-messaging connection closes. internal/cmd/serve.go implements this in NewWebSocketHandler, allowedOrigin, issueToken, and redeemToken.
scope_reason: The WebSocket boundary and token lifecycle are implemented together in the server file.

checklist.name: allowed-extension-origin-only
checklist.rule: WebSocket requests are accepted only from configured extension origins, and requests with a missing or non-matching Origin are refused. Return not applicable if the file does not define the PTY WebSocket boundary.

checklist.name: one-time-token-before-session
checklist.rule: The WebSocket handler validates a fresh one-time token bound to the tty id before looking up or exposing the terminal session. Return not applicable if the file does not define the PTY WebSocket boundary.

checklist.name: no-secret-echo-on-refusal
checklist.rule: Refusal paths do not echo the tty id, attach token, or other attach secrets in user-visible error messages. Return not applicable if the file does not define the PTY WebSocket boundary.
